Defend Public Lands
Giveaway with the Sitka Conservation Society & Liz Morrow

The U.S. Department of Agriculture is trying to remove the Roadless Rule — eliminating protections that prohibit road building and commercial logging on 44+ million acres of public land. For the past quarter century, this rule has safeguarded the headwaters that supply clean drinking water, ancient old-growth forests that act as our nation's lungs, and the lands that nurture traditional practices, hunting, fishing, and recreation for millions of Americans.

The Sitka Conservation Society is the oldest conservation organization in Alaska. Our mission is to protect the Tongass National Forest and support thriving communities across Southeast Alaska. Nine million acres of the Tongass are under threat of losing protections by repealing the Roadless Rule.

The Sitka Conservation Society has teamed up with artist Liz Morrow to offer gratitude for taking the time to speak up.
